name: AAGAM UX Redesign Proposals
prompt:
You are running as an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Saikumar-bali, owner of AAGAM_E-commerce. Propose a concrete UI/UX redesign for ONE screen of this product and open a review-only draft PR showing it as a static mockup.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT: this is a mockup pass, not a refactor. Do NOT change any shipped application code under apps/*. Do not touch routing, state, API calls, package.json, or native config. Your only changes are the mockup and proposal files. The default branch must stay shippable.

STEP 0 - PREPARE. Work from the cloned repository at main. Create a branch: git checkout -b ux-proposals/<yyyy-mm-dd> (add a short suffix if it already exists). Read AGENTS.md if present. Read packages/mobile-shared/src/constants/theme.ts - existing tokens and brand conventions are the starting point, not something to discard wholesale.

STEP 1 - PICK ONE SCREEN. Choose exactly ONE screen this run, and rotate: check recent branches and open PRs named ux-proposals/* to see what was proposed last, and pick something different. Prefer high-traffic, user-visible screens with real UX problems over cosmetic churn. Candidates: the customer subscription detail, the rider run detail flow, the store milk grid (MilkDeliveryGrid.tsx), checkout, order tracking. State clearly which screen you chose and why.

STEP 2 - DIAGNOSE WITH EVIDENCE. Read the actual screen implementation and identify concrete, specific UX problems - not vague opinions. Hold yourself to this standard: primary actions below the fold on a common device, tap targets under 44pt, unlabelled icon-only buttons, contrast under 4.5:1, missing loading/empty/error states, no offline handling, ambiguous money presentation, or flows that make the user guess the next step. Cite file and line for each problem. If you cannot cite it, do not claim it.

STEP 3 - DESIGN A BETTER VERSION. Apply the frontend-design skill deliberately. Commit to one clear aesthetic direction and justify it against the product's existing brand. Address every problem you diagnosed. Keep accessibility first-class: keyboard and screen-reader reachable controls, focus-visible styling, sufficient contrast, real labels rather than placeholder-only inputs, and reduced-motion respect. Aim for a distinctly better interface, not a generic AI restyle. Do not converge on the usual template look, and do not copy the current design back at itself.

STEP 4 - BUILD THE ARTIFACT.
Create automations/ux-proposals/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<screen>/proposal.md containing:
  - which screen, and the evidence for each diagnosed problem (file:line);
  - the aesthetic direction and why it fits this product;
  - an explicit before/after mapping: each problem, the change, and its expected effect;
  - an honest 'what I would need to verify before shipping this' list, including any measurement or accessibility check you could not run headlessly;
  - the token changes against packages/mobile-shared/src/constants/theme.ts.
Create automations/ux-proposals/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<screen>/mockup.html: ONE self-contained static HTML file, no build step, rendering the redesign side by side with the current screen so a reviewer can compare at a glance. Inline all CSS, add no dependencies, use a system font stack or a single embeddable webfont. Include at least the default, loading, empty, and error variants. Render accurately at 360px wide and at desktop width.

STEP 5 - VERIFY. Confirm the mockup HTML opens standalone and every state renders. Run `git status` and confirm you changed no shipped application code. If you find yourself editing anything under apps/*, stop and revert it.

STEP 6 - COMMIT AND OPEN A DRAFT PR. Commit with a clear message ending in: 'Co-authored-by: openhands <openhands@all-hands.dev>'. Push the branch and open a DRAFT pull request to main titled 'UX proposal: <screen> (<date>)'. In the PR body include the screen, the aesthetic direction, the before/after table, the token changes, and this exact note: '_This proposal contains static HTML mockups only and changes no application code. It is generated by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Saikumar-bali and is intended as a design discussion starting point, not as mergeable code._' Do not mark the PR ready for review. Do not merge it.

If you cannot produce a runnable mockup, say so plainly and open the proposal document alone rather than claiming a working artifact.
